findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand-new `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver, so logs emitted via `FromContext(ctx)` are recorded on a throwaway logger; `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` emits "Plugin Request Completed" this way, so existing tests asserting on the original `TestLogger` (e.g., logger middleware tests checking `InfoLogs.Calls`) will fail and the new logging path is unverifiable with this fake; it should return `f` (or share the same `Logs` structs)

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go — the new middleware ships with no tests in this diff; nothing verifies that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics attach `endpoint`/`pluginId`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` to the context, or that the streaming endpoints intentionally skip enrichment, even though `LoggerMiddleware`'s log output now depends entirely on this middleware being present and ordered correctly

[Low/bug] pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — `LoggerMiddleware` no longer emits `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` itself and now silently depends on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` being in the stack and ordered before it; any stack constructed with `NewLoggerMiddleware` alone (unit tests, other entry points building middleware lists directly) will produce "Plugin Request Completed" lines missing those fields with no error or warning signaling the misconfiguration

[Low/bug] pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:47 — the `.(*log.ConcreteLogger)` type assertion silently falls back to `d.New()` whenever infra's `FromContext` returns a different implementation, dropping all contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) from downstream logs with no signal; wrapping the returned `log.Logger` interface directly (changing the struct field type to the interface) would avoid this silent degradation path

[Low/api] pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23 — adding `FromContext` to the exported `Logger` interface is a breaking change for any out-of-tree implementer of `plog.Logger`; all implementers are now forced to provide a method whose semantics (merging contextual attributes from a `context.Context`) are not specified by the interface contract, which only says it returns "this logger's context plus the given context" (copy-pasted from `New`)

[Low/doc_defect] pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go (TestInstrumentationMiddleware) — the test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` after the file, type, and constructor were renamed to Metrics; the incomplete rename will confuse future greps, coverage mapping, and anyone reading the file

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go — the new middleware ships with no tests in this diff; nothing verifies that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics attach `endpoint`/`pluginId`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` to the context, or that the streaming endpoints intentionally skip enrichment, even though `LoggerMiddleware`'s log output now depends entirely on this middleware being present and ordered correctly

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (new file `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go`) that enriches the request `context.Context` via `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, while intentionally doing nothing for streaming endpoints. No corresponding test file/assertions are added in this diff to verify those context attributes are present or that streaming endpoints skip enrichment. This matters because `LoggerMiddleware` was changed to rely on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (and it no longer appends `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname`, etc. itself), so correct behavior now depends on this new middleware being present and ordered correctly (as wired in `CreateMiddlewares`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — `LoggerMiddleware` no longer emits `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` itself and now silently depends on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` being in the stack and ordered before it; any stack constructed with `NewLoggerMiddleware` alone (unit tests, other entry points building middleware lists directly) will produce "Plugin Request Completed" lines missing those fields with no error or warning signaling the misconfiguration

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, `logRequest` no longer receives `pluginCtx`/`endpoint` and the log params list explicitly removed `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname` (and traceID). It now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, which means those attributes will only appear if some earlier middleware has enriched `ctx` (e.g., the newly added `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` using `log.WithContextualAttributes`). While `CreateMiddlewares` now orders `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`, the coupling/ordering requirement is implicit and a stack using `NewLoggerMiddleware` without the contextual middleware will silently emit logs missing those fields. This is a real, diff-grounded design/configuration concern but not a demonstrable functional defect beyond reduced log enrichment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:47 — the `.(*log.ConcreteLogger)` type assertion silently falls back to `d.New()` whenever infra's `FromContext` returns a different implementation, dropping all contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) from downstream logs with no signal; wrapping the returned `log.Logger` interface directly (changing the struct field type to the interface) would avoid this silent degradation path

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, FromContext calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and then asserts the result to *log.ConcreteLogger; if the assertion fails it silently returns d.New() with no args. That fallback path clearly discards any context-derived attributes that infra’s FromContext would have applied (it creates a fresh wrapper without using ctx). The diff doesn’t prove that d.l.FromContext(ctx) can ever return a non-*log.ConcreteLogger, so the impact is an edge-case/robustness concern rather than a verifiable defect, but the silent degradation path is real in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23 — adding `FromContext` to the exported `Logger` interface is a breaking change for any out-of-tree implementer of `plog.Logger`; all implementers are now forced to provide a method whose semantics (merging contextual attributes from a `context.Context`) are not specified by the interface contract, which only says it returns "this logger's context plus the given context" (copy-pasted from `New`)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new method `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` to the exported `Logger` interface in `pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go`. In Go, adding a method to an interface is a source-breaking API change for any external (out-of-tree) type that previously implemented `plog.Logger`, since they must now implement `FromContext` to compile. The interface comment is also vague/copy-pasted (“has this logger's context plus the given context”), and the diff does not specify how contextual attributes are expected to be derived/merged from `context.Context` beyond that one-line doc, even though new middleware (`ContextualLoggerMiddleware`) relies on context-enriched logging.
